title: Beebe Vent Field: the deepest black smokers

briefing.summary: Descend to the Beebe Hydrothermal Vent Field on the Mid-Cayman Spreading Centre and scan its black-smoker chimneys and the Rimicaris shrimp swarms living around them. A western sulfide mound offers another nearby target.
facts: Beebe is the deepest known active hydrothermal vent field, confirmed at 4,957-4,987 m (Connelly et al. 2012, Nature Communications).
Its low-salinity vent fluid has been measured around 401–403 °C at roughly 500 bar, hot and pressurized enough to become supercritical.
Thousands of a shrimp new to science, Rimicaris hybisae, swarm the chimneys; it has no adult eyes but carries a light-sensing organ that may detect the vents' own faint glow.
The field sits on the Mid-Cayman Spreading Centre, the world's deepest and one of its slowest-spreading mid-ocean ridges (~15 mm/yr).
hazards: Rated depth: this Class C hull can operate to 11,000 m, giving wide margin here, but treat the pressure at nearly 5,000 m as real and unforgiving.
Scalding, chemically hostile fluid at the chimney mouths -- some of it supercritical, hotter than 400 degC. Do not linger inside a plume.
Total darkness; only your lights and the chimneys' own faint thermal signature illuminate anything here.
Von Damm, this ridge's other major vent field, lies about 13 km southwest at ~2,300 m -- well outside this survey's tile and not reachable in this mission.

objectives.title: Scan the Beebe 1-5 black smokers
objectives.hint: The Beebe 1–5 black-smoker complex is on the Mid-Cayman seafloor, close to 4,990 m.

objectives.title: Survey the Rimicaris hybisae swarm
objectives.hint: The Rimicaris hybisae swarm is beside the Beebe chimneys, around 4,980 m.

objectives.title: Survey the western sulfide mound
objectives.hint: The western sulfide mound is southwest of the main Beebe chimneys, near 4,960 m.
